newsitem.title: USA: Circuit City loses discrimination case.
newsitem.headline: Circuit City loses discrimination case.

text.p: A jury awarded compensation totaling nearly $290,000 against Circuit City Stores Inc. Monday after finding the electronics retailer guilty of failing to promote two black employees.
The Richmond-based company was ordered to pay $237,000 to one woman and $52,200 to a second plaintiff.
The suit started last year as a class action on behalf of 10 employees, later extended to 11, alleging that the company discriminated against African-Americans in promotions.
When the case went before the jury in a Richmond federal district court the number of plaintiffs had been reduced to three.
Circuit City said it was disappointed by the decision and planned to appeal.
"We continue to believe that the facts do not support individual discrimination against the two plaintiffs," chief executive officer Richard Sharp said in a statement.
"We are shocked that the jury could find a pattern and practice of discrimination while also finding in favor of only two plaintiffs in a case that began with 11 plaintiffs," he said.
